setup_name: Stocks in play on company news (opening phase)
universe_filter: stocks with a fresh catalyst: contract win, earnings upgrade/downgrade, trading update at AGM, broker rating change, or a large overnight move in the related commodity; ~20 names per day; mid caps preferred over sleepy large caps
conditions: catalyst published before the open
stock shows strong opening volume and liquidity
order book/price action confirms direction of the catalyst (buyers lifting offers for good news)
entry_trigger: discretionary timing off the order book and tape in the opening minutes, in the direction of the news
stop: tight; exit immediately if the trade does not move in favour straight away, hitting the visible bids behind the entry
target_or_exit: discretionary; ride the momentum, flat by the close
management: larger size with tight stop because well-timed catalyst trades are in profit quickly
stated_edge: A catalyst brings volume, liquidity and directional institutional flow, so risk/reward is much better than in names without news.
mcf_translation: Proxy catalyst with opening gap > ~3% and relative volume > 3 in the first 5-min bar; enter in gap direction on break of the first 5-min bar extreme; stop at the other side of that bar; time stop if not in profit after 2-3 bars; exit at close.

setup_name: Strong-market new-high momentum buy (52-week-high list)
time_of_day: after the first 15 minutes (from ~10:15), mainly first hour
universe_filter: stocks trading within 2-3% of their 52-week high (about 100 names), then filtered intraday to those at their day high; recently tech stocks
conditions: strong market lead-in: overseas market/index futures indicate roughly +1.5% for the session
market keeps trending up intraday
stock is at or very near its intraday high and near its 52-week high
entry_trigger: buy as the stock prints a new intraday high (break of high of day)
stop: not specified precisely; cut longs when the broad market rolls over
target_or_exit: hold while the market trends; exit when the market index rolls over or by the close
management: market exposure trade; position sized larger than order-book scalps because liquidity is deeper in trending strong stocks
stated_edge: With the market wind at your back, buying the strongest stocks at their highs gives momentum follow-through; reverse for weak markets (short weak stocks at their lows).
data_needed: none essential (needs index futures or SPY gap as market filter)
mcf_translation: Market filter: SPY gap > +1% (or SPY above VWAP and up > 1% by 9:45). Universe: daily close within 3% of 252-day high. After 9:45, go long when a 5-min bar breaks the session high; stop below session VWAP or the last 5-min swing low; exit when SPY loses its VWAP or at close. Mirror for shorts: SPY gap < -1%, stocks within 3% of 52-week low breaking session low.

setup_name: Overnight commodity move into resource stocks
instrument: stocks (resource/miners/energy), with US ETFs (GDX, GDXJ, XOP, XLE) as reference
universe_filter: resource stocks tied to a commodity that moved strongly overnight (e.g. nickel -6% on the LME), cross-checked against the related US-listed sector ETF move rather than the raw commodity
conditions: large overnight move in the commodity
related sector ETF confirms the move
stock still needs to qualify on order book/price action
entry_trigger: discretionary entry in the direction of the commodity move after the open
stop: tight, order-book based
target_or_exit: intraday, flat by close
management: not specified
stated_edge: Commodity moves are a strong lead-in catalyst for heavily resource-weighted markets; the sector ETF tells you if equities actually followed the commodity.
data_needed: commodity futures prices overnight; sector mapping of stocks
mcf_translation: For US stocks: when a sector ETF (GDX, XOP, XLE) gaps > 2%, trade member stocks in the gap direction on a first-15-minute range break; compare with a baseline of gap-and-go without sector confirmation.

setup_name: Bulge-bracket broker upgrade/downgrade follow-through
time_of_day: the session after the rating change
universe_filter: stocks upgraded or downgraded overnight by a major institutional broker (e.g. neutral to overweight), not a retail-only broker
conditions: rating change from a broker whose clients are institutions
stock may not have moved much on the original news
entry_trigger: trade in the direction of the rating change once the order book shows institutional flow
stop: tight, order-book based
target_or_exit: intraday
management: not specified
stated_edge: Institutional clients act on bulge-bracket research, producing sustained one-directional flow the next day.
data_needed: analyst rating change feed with broker identity
mcf_translation: Would need an analyst-ratings feed; then test gap direction plus first 30-min range break on rating-change days.

setup_name: Bollinger-band mean reversion with a minimum band width (volatility floor)
universe_filter: liquid instruments where intraday mean reversion is known to work
conditions: price stretches beyond a Bollinger band of the recent lookback
band width is never allowed below a fixed minimum volatility level, so quiet periods do not produce bands that are too narrow
alternatively shorten the lookback so the band adapts faster when volatility jumps
entry_trigger: fade a close beyond the band (buy below lower band, sell above upper band)
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: revert to the band mean
management: not specified; whatever change is made must be re-backtested
stated_edge: Plain Bollinger mean reversion loses when volatility rises suddenly and the band, set in calm conditions, is too narrow; a width floor or shorter lookback reduces that risk.
mcf_translation: On 5-min bars: z = (close - SMA20)/max(std20, k * median std20 over 20 days). Enter long when z < -2, exit at z >= 0 or at close. Compare with and without the floor; check whether the floor cuts drawdowns on volatility-jump days.

setup_name: Bollinger squeeze breakout to order-block targets
universe_filter: Bitcoin on the leading exchanges
conditions: price channelling sideways with Bollinger Bands contracting (range contraction)
order-block zones marked from prior candle wick/body clusters as horizontal rectangles
entry_trigger: range expansion: price breaks out of the band/channel; trade in the breakout/trend direction
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: take profit at the next order-block zone; flatten before sleeping
management: during strong trends, hold the trend position and scalp counter-trend consolidations around it
stated_edge: Bitcoin trends hard after periods of contraction, and price repeatedly reaches clusters of orders that larger players push into; few algorithms in this market, so classic TA works.
mcf_translation: Equity analogue: 5-min Bollinger band width at a 20-day low, then a close outside the band; target the prior day's high/low or a recent swing level; stop at the band midline. Testable on stocks if desired, but the guest's evidence is for Bitcoin only.

firm_or_style: HFT / fast alpha (example given by guest)
setup_name: Short-horizon pair divergence fade (e.g. two large-cap airlines)
instrument: US stocks (pairs in same industry and country)
universe_filter: highly similar large caps in the same industry, e.g. American vs United
conditions: the two stocks' prices diverge over a short window with no news
the divergence is assumed to be liquidity-driven, not information-driven
entry_trigger: buy the underperformer and short the outperformer when the short-term spread is stretched
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: spread converges
management: dollar- or beta-neutral pair
stated_edge: On short timescales, divergence between near-identical companies is usually temporary liquidity pressure, so fading it is fairly low risk.
data_needed: none for 5-min version (true version is sub-second)
mcf_translation: For hand-picked pairs (AAL/UAL, XOM/CVX, KO/PEP, etc.) compute 5-min log-price spread vs. its rolling 20-day intraday mean; z < -2 buy spread, z > 2 sell spread; exit at z = 0 or close; skip days with news gaps > 3% in either leg. Costs on both legs.

setup_name: Overextended multi-day runner, short the first crack
universe_filter: stocks up for 3-10 consecutive days without a real pullback; abnormal volume (millions of shares); large range
conditions: nightly scan for consecutive up days with no meaningful pullback
stock still on volume the next morning
first sign of profit taking: price cracks after the push
entry_trigger: short at the first crack, when holders first see a reason to take profits (first break of an intraday support/low after the extension)
stop: above the high of the move (tight, size small due to range)
target_or_exit: quick snap lower over 5-20 minutes; cover into the flush
management: start small, add only where a fresh short would make sense
stated_edge: After a long uninterrupted run nobody has a reason to sell; the first crack triggers widespread profit taking and a fast, predictable drop.
data_needed: short borrow availability/fees for realistic costs
mcf_translation: Daily filter: >= 3 consecutive higher closes, cumulative gain > 30%, price $1-20, 20-day avg volume > 1M and today rvol > 2. Intraday: after 9:35, short when a 5-min bar closes below the prior 5-min bar low after a new session high (or first close below VWAP); stop above session high; exit after 4 bars (20 min) or at -1R/+3R.

setup_name: Failed follow-through momentum short (prior-day resistance retest)
universe_filter: stock that has moved a lot recently and pulled back the prior day; high volume
conditions: big prior momentum move
stock pulled back on the prior day
next morning price rallies to retest the prior day's resistance (high area)
entry_trigger: short when the retest of prior-day resistance fails (price rejects and turns down)
stop: just above the prior-day resistance level
target_or_exit: fade and washout lower; cover into the flush
management: not specified
stated_edge: Momentum buyers fail to push through yesterday's resistance; trapped longs then sell and the stock fades.
mcf_translation: Universe: 5-day return > 30% and prior day close < prior day open. Intraday: if price trades within 1% of prior-day high in the first 60 min and a 5-min bar closes back below the prior-day high minus 1%, short; stop above the intraday high; target VWAP then prior-day low; exit at close.

setup_name: ABCD pullback long (higher base)
universe_filter: stocks in play with strong morning run and high relative volume
conditions: stock runs up (A to B)
pulls back and forms a higher base (C) above the prior low
starts to grind up off the base
entry_trigger: buy dips as it grinds up off the higher base
stop: below the base / prior low (C)
target_or_exit: back to the highs (B) and potential breakout; aims ~3:1 reward to risk
management: add only at levels where a fresh entry would make sense
stated_edge: A higher base after a run shows buyers are still in control; risk is defined by the base low while reward is a retest/breakout of the high.
mcf_translation: Gap > 4%, rvol > 3. Track session high (B) after 9:35; pullback low (C) must hold above 50% retracement of open-to-B; enter when a 5-min bar closes above prior bar high after C; stop below C; target B + (B - C) or 3R; exit at close.

setup_name: Opening washout reversal long on multi-day decliner
universe_filter: stocks that have been beaten down over several days (e.g. 24 to 16 over a week); high volume
conditions: multi-day decline with no bounce
panic flush at or shortly after the open
entry_trigger: buy the washout once selling exhausts and price reverses (reactive trade)
stop: below the washout low
target_or_exit: reversal bounce (e.g. from 14 back to 17 in the example)
management: quick trade, dale and bail
stated_edge: Buying when weak holders capitulate in a panic; emotional extremes create the reversal.
mcf_translation: Daily: >= 4 consecutive lower closes, drawdown > 25% from 10-day high. Intraday: open below prior close, new low in first 30 min, then a 5-min bar closes above the prior bar high and back above the open; buy; stop below low; target prior-day close or VWAP + 1 ATR; exit by close.

setup_name: Support pullback long with stochastic oversold, scaled exits at +3%/+5%
time_of_day: entries pre-market/open or into the close; holds 1 hour to 5 days
universe_filter: weekend scan of daily charts; ~8 ideas per week (4 long, 4 short) checked on weekly/monthly charts
conditions: price near medium-term support on the daily chart
slow stochastic near oversold
weekly/monthly chart does not contradict
entry_trigger: small first entry near support; add on a successful retest of support or as it keeps working (4-5 scales to full size)
stop: hard stop placed at entry, max loss 1% of position value
target_or_exit: sell one scale at +3%, the next at +5%; leave a quarter to a fifth on while it holds above +5%
management: hold overnight only if the stock closes within roughly the top 10% of the day's move; exit on weak closes
stated_edge: Buying close to support gives a clear stop and favourable risk; scaling and partial profits pay for the trade.
mcf_translation: Daily: close within 2% above 20-day low or a prior swing low, slow stochastic(14,3) < 20. Enter next open; stop 1% below support level (or fixed -1% of entry as stated); exit 1/3 at +3%, 1/3 at +5%, rest when daily close location value (close-low)/(high-low) < 0.9 or after 5 days.

setup_name: Range trading established intraday/multi-day ranges
universe_filter: stocks that have bounced between two levels (e.g. $9-$10) for hours or days, often in a sector that is basing after a drop
conditions: clear, repeated range top and bottom
range has held several times
entry_trigger: short near the top of the range, cover at the bottom; buy at the bottom, sell at the top
stop: just beyond the range edge (hard stop)
target_or_exit: opposite side of the range
management: keep doing it until the range breaks; the main risk is stubbornly fighting a breakout
stated_edge: Consistent ranges repeat until they break; defined edges give clear risk.
stated_stats: often 4-5 green days followed by one stubborn losing day
mcf_translation: Identify a range on 5-min bars: last 3 sessions high-low within 10% and at least 2 touches of each edge (within 0.5%). Fade touches of the edge with stop 0.5% beyond; target opposite edge minus 10% of width; disable after the first close outside the range.

setup_name: Short the less-crowded outliers of a hot sector rotation at resistance
universe_filter: secondary names in a sector receiving a burst of money (solar, semis, China names, biotech), not the crowded leaders
conditions: sector runs hot quickly
outlier stock spikes into a clear chart resistance level
stock appears to peak
entry_trigger: short near the resistance level as the move stalls
stop: hard stop just above resistance
target_or_exit: fade back down; scaled exits
management: avoid crowded shorts where moves are forced
stated_edge: Outliers in a hot sector overshoot and fade more naturally than crowded leaders, whose moves are distorted by heavy positioning.
mcf_translation: Sector ETF 5-day return in top decile; pick member stocks outside the top 3 by volume with 5-day return > 20%; short when daily high is within 1% of a 60-day high/resistance and close is in the lower half of the day's range; stop above high; exit after 3-5 days or at 10-day MA.

setup_name: Moving-average remount after a stop run
universe_filter: stocks in line with or leading the market, in sectors receiving money flow; watchlist names respecting a key moving average
conditions: stock has been holding a widely watched moving average (e.g. 20/50-day)
price dips below the moving average, triggering the crowd's stops (stop gunning)
price then reclaims (remounts) the moving average
entry_trigger: buy when price moves back above the moving average after the shake-out; alternatively take a half position before and add on the remount
stop: below the shake-out low, allowing for normal volatility
target_or_exit: pre-planned target at resistance, about 3:1 reward/risk
management: set and forget; do not micromanage on lower timeframes
stated_edge: Market makers and algorithms know where moving-average stops cluster and push through them; once those stops are flushed, the move resumes and the remount gives a cleaner entry.
mcf_translation: Daily: close above 50-day SMA for >= 10 of the last 15 days; then a day with low < SMA50 * 0.99 and close back above SMA50 (or next-day close back above). Enter at close/next open; stop below the shake-out low; target 3R or prior swing high; time stop 15 days. Intraday variant: 5-min bar dips below session VWAP or prior-day low by > 0.3% then closes back above it.

setup_name: Hold quality longs through a macro gap-down (mental stop)
time_of_day: open of a market-wide gap-down session
universe_filter: strong existing long positions (e.g. post-earnings breakouts) when the whole market gaps down on outside news
conditions: gap down caused by an external macro event not specific to the stock
gap has gone through the planned stop
stock holds the gap level after the open
entry_trigger: no new entry; keep the position (or add) if the gap level holds and price starts to bounce
stop: mental stop: exit if the gap-down low fails
target_or_exit: original target, or recovery of part/all of the gap
management: use mental rather than hard stops on such days if you can watch; part-timers with hard stops will be taken out
stated_edge: Panic gaps on unrelated news are often overreactions that reverse once traders reassess; selling at the open is selling with the weakest hands.
mcf_translation: On days SPY gaps < -1.5%, for stocks held in an MCF swing book: compare exiting at the open vs. holding with a stop at the first-30-minute low. Measure next-day and 5-day outcome.

setup_name: Pre-planned level with price-ladder (order book) confirmation
universe_filter: two main futures contracts with macro bias set first
conditions: macro/fundamental bias defined
price approaches a pre-planned support/resistance level from the bigger picture
on the ladder: sellers lose aggression, bids are reloaded at the level (e.g. a 200-lot bid replenished as it is hit) rather than pulled
entry_trigger: buy (or sell) at the planned level once the ladder confirms real interest defending it
stop: beyond the level / structure, not a tiny 3-4 tick stop
target_or_exit: next profile or chart level
management: stand aside if the ladder shows bids pulled or aggressive selling through the level
stated_edge: Price ladder behaviour shows whether the planned level is genuinely defended; it is the final checklist item that separates profitable from marginal prop traders.
mcf_translation: Not testable with bars. Bar-only proxy: buy at a pre-computed support (prior-day low or value-area low) only if the 5-min bar touching it closes in its upper half on above-average volume.

setup_name: Value-area / point-of-control balance and shift (market profile)
instrument: futures (Euro Stoxx, Bund); applicable to liquid stocks/ETFs
universe_filter: liquid instruments
conditions: market trades around a perceived value (POC) with little range for a period (balance)
a shift occurs when price leaves the value area and builds volume at new prices
context: fundamental news and correlated markets
entry_trigger: trade in the direction of a value shift once price accepts outside prior value; or fade overshoots back toward value while balance holds
stop: back inside the old value area (for shifts) or beyond the overshoot extreme (for fades)
target_or_exit: new value area / next high-volume node; for fades, the POC
management: reassess where value is through the day
stated_edge: Markets are an auction seeking value; profile shows where participants accept price and when that acceptance moves, which candles alone do not show.
data_needed: tick or 1-min volume-at-price for accurate profiles (5-min approximation possible)
mcf_translation: Build a rolling volume profile from 5-min bars (distribute bar volume across its high-low range). Prior-day value area = 70% volume around POC. Long if price opens inside prior value, then two consecutive 5-min closes above prior VAH (acceptance); stop back below VAH; target VAH + prior VA width. Mirror for shorts. Fade variant: price opens outside value and re-enters it: target POC (80% rule).

firm_or_style: NYSE floor broker for a hedge fund
setup_name: Closing auction imbalance trade
universe_filter: NYSE stocks with published closing buy/sell imbalances; heavier on rebalance, expiry and month-end days
conditions: projected closing imbalance information available from ~14:00
large one-sided imbalance indicating direction into the close
entry_trigger: take positions (long or short stocks/SPY) in the direction of the projected closing imbalance in the afternoon
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: exit all positions at the 16:00 closing print
management: flat at the close
stated_edge: Imbalance flow that must execute at the close is visible to floor brokers in advance and pushes prices in its direction into the bell.
mcf_translation: Without imbalance data, a crude proxy: on known rebalance days (quarterly S&P, monthly Russell) and month-end, test the direction of the 15:00-16:00 move vs. the 09:30-15:00 move.

firm_or_style: NYSE floor broker for a hedge fund
setup_name: Overnight reversal (flip) after an extreme close
time_of_day: enter at the close, exit next morning
universe_filter: index or index components after a very large daily move
conditions: market closes with a huge spike up (e.g. Dow +500) or a big sell-off
entry_trigger: at the close, take a small position against the day's move (short after a big up close, long after a big down close)
stop: not specified (small size)
target_or_exit: exit in the next morning's trading
management: small size, separate from the flat-by-close day book
stated_edge: Extreme closes tend to see partial reversal at the next open.
mcf_translation: SPY: if close-to-close return > +2% (or < -2%), enter opposite at the close; exit at next day's open or 10:00. Also test thresholds of 1.5 sigma of 20-day return volatility. Check sign stability across years.

setup_name: Fade the first move after the non-farm payrolls release
universe_filter: 10-year note futures on NFP days
conditions: NFP release triggers a sharp initial move in either direction
observation that after a few minutes the move often reverses hard (stated as a hypothesis to verify)
entry_trigger: take the opposite side of the first post-release move (sell the initial spike, buy the initial drop)
stop: to be determined by research (size of initial move)
target_or_exit: reversal over the following minutes; possibly time-based exit
management: research should measure magnitude dependence and whether a stop helps
stated_edge: Hypothesised overreaction to the headline number; explicitly presented as needing data verification.
stated_stats: market about four times more volatile on payroll days (example claim to verify)
data_needed: pre-market/futures data at 8:30 ET (MCF regular-hours bars miss the release)
mcf_translation: With regular-hours data only: on NFP days, if SPY/TLT open gap direction (reflecting 8:30 reaction) exceeds 0.5%, fade the first 5-min bar's direction after 9:35; exit at 10:30. Proper test needs futures 1-min data around 8:30.

setup_name: Earnings straddle relative-value from historical straddle ranges
universe_filter: optionable stocks with earnings coming, e.g. Microsoft
conditions: record historical at-the-money straddle prices around past earnings
compare current straddle to its historical low/high range before earnings
entry_trigger: buy the straddle when it is cheap vs. its historical pre-earnings range; sell it when too rich
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: not specified (typically through or around the earnings event)
management: not specified
stated_edge: Historical implied-volatility data across stocks shows when event premium is mispriced.
mcf_translation: Not testable without options data. A stock-only proxy: compare realised earnings-day move vs. historical average to flag names whose moves are systematically larger than typical.

setup_name: Market-profile single-print / gap fill (market seeks balance)
instrument: futures (crude oil); concept applies to liquid ETFs/stocks
universe_filter: crude oil futures
conditions: TPO profile shows single prints (thin, one-time-traded zones) or gaps from a fast move
rotation levels, Fibonacci levels and volume profile mark where real buyers and sellers are
footprint shows who is aggressive
entry_trigger: trade toward the single-print zone expecting it to be filled as the market balances
stop: tight, beyond the nearest rotation level
target_or_exit: fill of the single-print area
management: same trades repeated daily; 3-5 trades max
stated_edge: Markets tend to rebalance and revisit thin, low-volume areas left by fast moves.
mcf_translation: From 5-min bars, mark low-volume nodes: price bands traded in only one 30-min period during a fast move (single-print proxy). When price returns within 0.3% of a band edge and the band is unfilled, enter toward the band's far edge; stop 0.3% beyond entry rotation level; target band fully traversed. Test on SPY/QQQ/USO.

setup_name: Crude seasonal: refinery-maintenance weakness, driving-season strength
universe_filter: crude oil
conditions: March: refinery maintenance season tends to bring crude inventory builds (bearish)
late April to June: debt redeterminations for producers plus summer driving demand may support prices
only a bull market above long-term chart resistance
entry_trigger: no precise trigger given; bias for day trades and swings
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: not specified
management: used as directional bias rather than a mechanical trade
stated_edge: Seasonal refinery and demand patterns shift supply/demand balance at predictable times of year.
data_needed: long history of crude or USO daily data
mcf_translation: Daily USO/XLE: compare mean return in March vs. late April-June over available years; if consistent, use as a bias filter on intraday energy setups (longs only in favourable season).

setup_name: Fibonacci confluence reversal with moving-average trigger
instrument: futures and FX (indexes, bonds, metals, oil, FX, grains); applicable to ETFs
horizon: swing (days; average a couple of days, up to 6 weeks)
time_of_day: entries near the session open (London or US); none late in the session
universe_filter: 36 liquid futures/FX markets scanned top-down on monthly, weekly and daily charts
conditions: price approaching a zone where three measures agree: Fibonacci retracement of the prior swing, Fibonacci extension of the corrective swing, and swing-expansion symmetry (next swing equal to or 1.618x the prior)
harmonic pattern completion at the zone
no major scheduled news event pending
entry_trigger: lower-timeframe (e.g. hourly) moving-average crossover/close in the reversal direction at the confluence zone
stop: beyond the confluence zone
target_or_exit: exit on a close below the 50-period moving average (for longs; above for shorts); take profit per rules
management: move the stop only after the market makes a new high (long) or new low (short); max 3% total open risk
stated_edge: Measured moves and Fibonacci ratios reflect how algorithmic and trend-following systems are programmed, so confluent levels attract reactions; rules remove emotion in volatile markets.
data_needed: futures data for her actual markets (ETFs as proxies)
mcf_translation: On daily bars of liquid ETFs (SPY, TLT, GLD, USO, etc.): find last swing (zigzag 5%); zone = overlap of 61.8% retracement and 1.0x/1.618x equal-move projection within 1%. When price enters the zone, go long on first 60-min close above 20-period hourly SMA (from 5-min bars) within the first 2 hours of the session; stop below zone low; trail stop to each new swing low only after a new high; exit on daily close below 50-day SMA or after 30 days.

setup_name: Long-only oversold mean reversion with market-trend filter
instrument: US stocks (S&P 500 constituents; also ASX 500, Russell 2000)
time_of_day: end-of-day signals; limit orders placed for the next session
universe_filter: historical S&P 500 constituents (survivorship-free); liquid names
conditions: stock severely oversold/stretched over the short term (rubber band stretched)
US market not trending down (index filter; stands aside in cash during downtrends)
many signals daily; up to ~100 limit orders placed, only 20 fills accepted
entry_trigger: next-day buy limit orders below the prior close on oversold names; once 20 positions fill, cancel the rest and exit any excess fills immediately
stop: not specified in the episode
target_or_exit: exit on the snap-back (uses the open price to exit in some systems)
management: max 20 concurrent positions; API manages fills overnight
stated_edge: Prices stretched far in one direction tend to snap back; high trade count (500-1000/yr) gives a consistent edge and quick drawdown recovery; works best in sideways or slowly rising markets.
stated_stats: US version about +14.5-15% net in 2015 while the S&P was flat; 600-700 trades/yr on Russell 2000; win rates typically 60%+
mcf_translation: Daily: SPY close > 200-day SMA (regime). Signal: close > 100-day SMA (long-term up) and 3-day RSI < 15 (or 3-day decline > 2 x ATR(10)). Next day buy limit at close - 0.5*ATR(10). Rank by RSI, cap 20 positions. Exit next open after close > previous day high (or RSI3 > 50), or after 5 days. Stress test: +/-20% parameters, randomised fills.

setup_name: Cross-sectional momentum ranking (top 20 strongest)
universe_filter: S&P 500 constituents (historical membership)
conditions: rank all constituents by trailing return; he uses 200 days (anything from 30 days up to 1 year works; under 30 days behaves mean-reverting)
market regime filter on the index
entry_trigger: buy the 20 strongest by rank
stop: exit when no longer in the top ranks / trend fails
target_or_exit: rebalance periodically; hold while the stock stays strong
management: equal positions; cut losers, let winners run
stated_edge: Relative strength persists over 1-12 months; cutting losers and letting winners run creates positive expectancy.
mcf_translation: Monthly: rank universe by 200-day ROC; hold top 20 while SPY > 200-day SMA; else cash. Compare 63, 126, 252-day lookbacks for parameter stability.

setup_name: GLD 1.5% up-day close-to-next-day short (cited as a NON-robust pattern)
time_of_day: buy at close, flip at next open, exit at next close
universe_filter: gold ETF only
conditions: GLD rallies more than 1.5% on the day
entry_trigger: buy at the close; next morning exit the long and go short at the open
stop: none stated
target_or_exit: cover the short at that day's close
management: none
stated_edge: None claimed: the guest uses it as an example of a single-market curve fit, because the same rule is terrible on S&P 500 stocks.
stated_stats: works very well on the gold ETF alone; fails on S&P 500 constituents
mcf_translation: Use as a robustness check for MCF's own validation tooling: test on GLD and on a broad stock universe; a rule should only pass if it is profitable across the universe, not one symbol.

setup_name: PS60: 60-minute pivot confirmation with room to the next supply/demand zone
instrument: US stocks (high-beta: TSLA, NFLX, AAPL, FB, GOOGL, AMZN, PCLN, BIDU, etc.)
time_of_day: hourly candles from 10:00 ET; any of the six intervals
universe_filter: high-beta, wide-range, liquid names that can be traded both long and short in one day
conditions: 60-minute chart with 5/10/20/50/100/150/200 EMA and SMA, Bollinger bands and a 30-period linear regression line marked as supply/demand zones
a pivot: price pushes against a supply (or demand) zone
the next 60-minute candle confirms by building above the prior candle's high (long) or below its low (short)
enough room before the next zone (e.g. several dollars on a high-beta name, not 30-40 cents)
stock acting in line with or stronger than index futures for longs (weaker for shorts)
entry_trigger: break and hold above the prior 60-minute candle high after confirmation (long); below the prior candle low (short)
stop: back inside the prior hourly range / below the pivot candle
target_or_exit: next supply/demand zone; take partial profit and hold a runner
management: break-even stop on the runner; skip trades without room
stated_edge: Hourly candles filter out the noise of retail traders on 1-minute charts; most attempts fail for small losses but confirmed pivots with room produce large runs (the 'Barry Sanders effect').
stated_stats: many small stops, a few large winners per day
mcf_translation: Build 60-min bars from 5-min. Long when a 60-min bar closes above the prior 60-min bar high AND the next bar trades above that bar's high (confirmation), provided distance to the nearest overhead level among {SMA/EMA 5-200 on 60-min, upper Bollinger(20,2), LR30} > 1.5 x ATR(60-min, 14); also require SPY 60-min return >= 0. Stop at the confirmation bar low; exit half at the next level, rest at close or break-even stop. Mirror for shorts. Universe: top-20 by beta and dollar volume.

setup_name: Daily range breakout from nightly scan, entry at prior-day high with 1% fixed risk
instrument: US stocks (S&P 500 and Russell 1000 names; any price)
time_of_day: next session after the scan; any time the level breaks
universe_filter: nightly review of ~500 charts (S&P 500, IWM members) for 6-10 stocks coming out of a daily range
conditions: stock has been in a range for at least 5-7 days (longer is better)
it closes above the range's supply level (or below demand for shorts)
next supply level is far enough above to justify the trade
entry_trigger: next day, buy when price takes out the prior day's high (e.g. prior high 25.00 with close 24.75)
stop: prior day's close (risk = entry - prior close)
target_or_exit: next supply level; take cash flow on part, hold a runner
management: position size = 1% of account / (entry - prior close); break-even stop on runner; can hold multiple days
stated_edge: Orderly multi-day bases resolve into organic moves with natural buyers; tight risk from the prior close gives large reward multiples.
mcf_translation: Daily: 7-day range (high-low)/close < 8%; today close > 7-day high. Next day: buy stop at today's high; stop = today's close; size by 1% risk; exit half at +2R, rest trailed at break-even then 10-day low; max hold 10 days. Shorts mirror.

setup_name: Multi-parameter long-term trend following (100-300 day lookbacks), long and short
instrument: futures (120 markets) and single stocks/stock futures
universe_filter: all liquid markets traded with identical rules
conditions: price trending above (long) or below (short) long-term moving averages / breakouts
run several copies of the system with lookbacks from about 100 to 300 days (e.g. 100, 150, 200, 250, 300)
entry_trigger: buy new highs / price crossing above the moving average (sell new lows / cross below), per lookback
stop: initial stop not too tight and not too wide (an 'optimal' loss, keeps win rate around 40%); trailing exit on the opposite signal or moving-average breach
target_or_exit: no target; exit on trailing stop / reverse signal
management: add to winners, never add to losers; volatility-based sizing; diversified across sectors
stated_edge: Momentum persists and big trends supply all the profit; diversification across many uncorrelated markets and both directions controls risk.
stated_stats: win rate low 40s; avg win 2-3x avg loss; 5-10% of trades produce all profits; Turtles made ~200%/yr 1985-87 at very high leverage
data_needed: futures data for the full version; MCF daily stock/ETF data covers a stock/ETF version
mcf_translation: Daily ETFs/stocks: for each lookback L in {100,150,200,250,300}: long when close > L-day high of prior L days (or above SMA_L), exit when close < SMA_L/2 lookback low; equal risk per sub-system, ATR-based sizing; include shorts. Measure win rate, payoff and sample size, and check parameter stability across L.

setup_name: The Squeeze: Bollinger bands inside Keltner channels, trade with the trend
time_of_day: any; uses 30-minute, hourly, daily and weekly charts
universe_filter: liquid stocks and index futures; scannable
conditions: Bollinger bands (20, 2 default) contract inside the Keltner channels (default settings) = volatility compression after a prior move
an existing trend (uptrend for longs, downtrend for shorts)
entry_trigger: enter in the trend direction as the squeeze resolves (bands expand back outside the Keltner channels) and momentum turns in the trend direction
stop: below the consolidation/swing low for longs (not specified precisely)
target_or_exit: sell most of the position (e.g. 7 of 10 contracts) at the 1.272 Fibonacci extension of the last swing; remainder toward 1.618 extension; or exit at the options-implied expected move
management: move stop to break-even after the first target; earliest planned exit two days after entry unless stopped
stated_edge: Markets move in pops and then rest; compression after a move signals the next move, which tends to continue the prevailing trend.
stated_stats: claims roughly an 87% chance the existing trend continues after a squeeze; 1.272 extension reached about 90% of the time, 1.618 about 50%
mcf_translation: Daily (or 60-min from 5-min) bars: squeeze_on = BB(20,2) upper < KC(20,1.5 ATR) upper and BB lower > KC lower. Trend = close > SMA50 (long). Enter when squeeze_on turns off and 12-bar momentum (close - midline of Donchian/SMA) > 0. Stop below last 10-bar low. Exit 70% at 1.272 extension of the prior swing (low to high, projected from the pullback low), move stop to entry, rest at 1.618 or after 10 days.

setup_name: Heavily shorted stock intraday reversal (short-squeeze momentum)
time_of_day: intraday after the reversal; held into the close, half overnight
universe_filter: stocks with short interest above ~20% of float (TSLA was ~40%) after a prolonged decline and bearish consensus
conditions: stock opens weak (e.g. down $10) then reverses sharply positive (up $5) on news or a surprise announcement
consistently high volume; every pullback bought
no chart resistance nearby (room to the next level)
entry_trigger: buy after the reversal turns the stock positive on the day, starting small
stop: not stated (initially small size limits risk)
target_or_exit: hold into the close; sell half at the close and hold half overnight for a possible gap
management: add repeatedly as the trade works (100 to 1,000 contracts in the example); step away from the screen during pullbacks to avoid emotional exits
stated_edge: Big moves happen when many people are wrong and must cover; heavy short interest plus a surprise forces short covering on top of new buying.
stated_stats: single-day profit about $1.4M on TSLA in Jan 2014 (after a $100k loss earlier that day)
mcf_translation: Without short interest: stocks down > 20% over 20 days; intraday open < prior close by > 3%, then price crosses above prior close with rvol > 3 by 11:00; buy on the cross; stop at session VWAP; exit half at close, rest next day open. Add a short-interest filter if MCF obtains SI data.

setup_name: ATR-exhaustion fade back toward VWAP (range-day mean reversion)
time_of_day: after enough of the day's range has been made; mostly regular session
universe_filter: E-mini S&P only
conditions: day's range so far >= 40% of the 14-day ATR (true on ~94% of days)
price near the predicted daily range extreme (a level that ~80% of days do not exceed, given range done in the morning)
price stretched away from VWAP
no news shock driving the move; proprietary breadth/tape algorithm not contradicting
entry_trigger: fade at the pre-computed level (limit order); do not chase if price stops a few ticks short
stop: about 3x the average 1-minute bar range (about 6-8 ES points)
target_or_exit: first scale at ~3-4 points (or quicker in slow markets), second scale at 7-9 points / VWAP
management: two scales; if price runs ~3 points against and returns to break-even, take off half; full size at entry, no averaging
stated_edge: Most index days are range days; once a typical day's range is made, further extension is less likely and HFT/market-making flow pulls price back toward VWAP.
stated_stats: losses average ~1 point, average trade ~4.5 points; first scale avg ~2.5 pts, second ~7 pts; roughly 2:1 win rate (March sample)
data_needed: futures data ideal; SPY 5-min sufficient for the concept
mcf_translation: SPY 5-min: ATR14 daily; condition session range >= 0.4*ATR14 and price at session high/low with distance from VWAP > 0.5*ATR14 (or at the 80th-percentile range level from history given time-of-day range). Fade with stop = entry +/- max(3 * avg 1-min range ~ 0.25*ATR14); exit half at 0.35*ATR14 or VWAP-halfway, rest at VWAP; flat by close. Skip days with gap > 1 ATR or scheduled news.

setup_name: Fast spike fade (large move in under an hour)
time_of_day: any; occurs mainly in high-volatility regimes
universe_filter: E-mini S&P
conditions: ES moves about 22+ points (handles) in less than one hour
high-volatility regime (such spikes are rare in calm markets)
entry_trigger: fade the spike after it prints
stop: about 3x the average 1-minute bar range
target_or_exit: about 5 points of reversion
management: two scales as in his core strategy
stated_edge: Fast, outsized spikes in the index tend to partially revert.
stated_stats: ~70% chance of reverting about 5 points after a 22-handle spike in under an hour (15 years of data)
mcf_translation: SPY 5-min: if |close - close 12 bars earlier| > 1.0% (about 22 ES points at a 2,000 index; scale to current level: 0.9-1.1%), enter opposite on the next bar; target 0.22% reversion; stop 0.45%; time stop 60 min. Report hit rate by volatility regime.

setup_name: Prior-day high/low and pivot as high-probability targets
instrument: futures (ES); applicable to SPY and liquid stocks
universe_filter: index futures
conditions: prior-day high or low is touched on ~88% of days
floor pivot traded on ~70% of days
use these as targets/magnets combined with range stats, not as stand-alone entries
entry_trigger: used to set targets and refine fade entries
stop: per core strategy
target_or_exit: the untouched prior-day extreme or pivot
management: n/a
stated_edge: Base rates of level touches give targets with known probabilities.
stated_stats: prior-day high or low hit ~88% of days; pivot ~70%
mcf_translation: Compute in MCF: daily probability of touching prior-day high, prior-day low, either, and pivot (H+L+C)/3 for SPY and each universe stock, conditioned on open location (inside vs outside prior range). Use as exit targets for existing MCF setups.

setup_name: Russell reconstitution closing-move trade (edge now gone)
time_of_day: last ~4 minutes before the close on Russell rebalance day
universe_filter: stocks with large expected index-driven market-on-close imbalances on the annual Russell rebalance day
conditions: custom filter of names likely to have big MOC moves
entry_trigger: buy or sell in the last four minutes in the direction of the expected close imbalance
stop: not specified
target_or_exit: exit on the closing print
management: none
stated_edge: Index-driven MOC flow moved prices at the close; the guest says the edge has since been arbitraged away.
stated_stats: profitable for a couple of years; no longer works
data_needed: index reconstitution add/delete lists, closing auction data
mcf_translation: Low priority given the guest's report that it no longer works; could be checked with Russell add/delete lists and 15:55-16:00 bars.

setup_name: Passive order-flow 'low-frequency market making' (absorb aggression, exit into exhaustion)
universe_filter: single-venue, deep futures order books
conditions: aggressive one-sided market orders hitting a level (read from order book and tape)
the aggression fails to move price (absorption)
book details: queue position, icebergs, thickness of book, cadence of volume
entry_trigger: bid passively under aggressive sellers (or offer above aggressive buyers) at the level
stop: small, a few ticks (risks slightly more than the typical win)
target_or_exit: one tick or so; exit into the trapped side's reaction
management: high win rate required; scratch quickly
stated_edge: Psychological inefficiency: aggressive traders who fail to move price become nervous and exit, giving the passive side a quick tick.
stated_stats: high win rate, small average win
data_needed: Level 2 order book, tick-by-tick trades, futures data
mcf_translation: Not testable with 5-min bars.

setup_name: Non-predictive multi-market strategy with edge from volatility-adaptive risk model
universe_filter: broad diversified futures universe
conditions: entries treated as essentially random ('the entry means nothing')
position size scaled to volatility
many concurrent positions across markets and strategies with different holding periods
entry_trigger: any systematic segmentation of the market into trade events (entry not the edge)
stop: volatility-based stop defining a fixed fraction of equity
target_or_exit: average winner significantly larger than average loser (payout asymmetry), e.g. 2:1 or more
management: keep bet size small; adapt to volatility; diversify by strategy and periodicity
stated_edge: Mathematical risk advantage: with many independent bets, payout odds and sizing can create positive expectancy even near 50% win rate.
data_needed: broader futures universe for the full version
mcf_translation: Useful as an MCF null/baseline: on the daily stock/ETF universe, random entries with ATR stops of 1 ATR and targets of 2-3 ATR (or trailing exits), vol-scaled size; compare against MCF setups to show how much edge is entry vs. exit/risk structure. Include costs.

setup_name: 52-week high/low breakout with EPS filter and Donchian trailing exit (long and short)
horizon: position (winners 3-6 months; losers 1-2 months or less)
time_of_day: enter at the US market open after an evening scan
universe_filter: Finviz scan: new 52-week highs (longs) or 52-week lows (shorts), decent average volume, rising EPS for longs (falling EPS for shorts)
conditions: the same stock reappears on the scan repeatedly (persistent strength/weakness)
smooth trend on the 1-2 year daily chart, bottom-left to top-right, without big whipsaws
entry_trigger: buy (short) at the next open after selection; no waiting for pullbacks
stop: initial stop at the Donchian channel (20 to 40-day low for longs / high for shorts), computed the night before to set size
target_or_exit: trailing Donchian channel stop (20-40 day) adjusted after each close; exits only when stopped
management: risk 2-4% of equity per trade (higher for smoother charts); max about eight positions; balance longs and shorts; diversify sectors; identical rules for every stock, shorts mirror longs
stated_edge: Turtle-style trend following: cutting losses small and letting the few big trends run produces a positive expectancy.
stated_stats: many small losers, few big winners; profitable over two to three years (no numbers given)
data_needed: EPS history (fundamental) for the earnings filter
mcf_translation: Daily: long candidate when close = 252-day high on at least 3 of the last 10 days, 50-day avg volume > 500k, (optional) trailing EPS growth > 0. Enter next open. Stop and trailing exit = 30-day lowest low (test 20/40). Risk 2% per trade, max 8 positions, cap net long/short imbalance at 2 positions. Shorts mirror with 252-day lows. Smoothness filter: R-squared of 252-day log-price regression > 0.7.

setup_name: Energy calendar-spread and butterfly mean reversion
instrument: futures (WTI, Brent calendar spreads, flies, condors)
horizon: intraday to swing (minutes to days; longer-dated flies take days)
universe_filter: WTI and Brent calendar spreads across maturities
conditions: spread trades in a range; spreads often react to big technical levels and moving averages
fundamental drivers (supply, sanctions, production cuts, war risk) shape outright moves that feed into spreads
wider-dated spreads (e.g. Dec/Dec) move faster than adjacent months
entry_trigger: discretionary entry at levels, executed via an auto-spreader so all legs fill at once
stop: monetary stop like an outright trade
target_or_exit: mean reversion within the spread's range
management: adjust multi-leg positions by lifting or replacing the losing leg
stated_edge: Synthetic spreads are more mean-reverting and less volatile than outrights, with more size on bids and offers.
stated_stats: example: spread daily range ~26 ticks vs ~200 for the outright
data_needed: futures term-structure data by contract month
mcf_translation: Not testable with MCF stock data. A rough equity analogue is pairs mean reversion between closely related ETFs (USO/BNO) on 5-min bars.
